event_name: UFC Fight Night: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker
notes: Hand-transcribed from the UFC Predictions Tracker's pre-event roundup for UFC Vegas 124 (Meta APEX, Las Vegas, 7 Nov 2026). The roundup was available only as a spoken transcript, which reports headcounts and never channel names, so it cannot be ingested as named picks — see src/mma_engine/tallies.py. Every count below is a number the host stated; fighter spellings were corrected against the official card. Panels this card: 7 best predictors, 6 best favorite-pickers, 7 best underdog-pickers, and a best-method panel of only 1 to 4 channels, which the host said was still filling in. Bout order follows the host's walk through the card; outlets disagree on where the prelims end.
Welterweight. One of the host's best bets, though he warns both men have fought rarely and recently enough that there is little to read.
Welterweight; Ko is the biggest favorite on the card at -705.

FLAG — no moneyline is recorded for this fight. The host said every channel picked Ko but never said how many channels that was, and a headcount nobody stated is not one this engine will invent. Every panel is 100% on Ko, and all 45 method votes are for him, so treat the moneyline as unanimous; the Moneylines tab simply has no count to show.
Middleweight. The host's first best bet: every panel 100% on Kondratavicius and 94% of the method votes a KO, which pays -165 against a -295 moneyline.
The best method predictors were also unanimous on that KO, but the host never gave the panel's size for this fight, so no method-panel count is recorded.

Featherweight. Calderon took this on four days' notice after Lucas Brennan tore an ACL, so the sample is a third of the card's: 29 channels on the winner, 19 on the method, one best-method predictor, and no method prices posted yet.
The host gave the submission count as "15 out of 90", which cannot be right against a 29-channel field; 19 is what his own split sums to and is used here.
He said the few best predictors who had posted were all on Bashi but gave no panel sizes, so no sharp counts are recorded.
Featherweight, and close everywhere: -116/-103 in odds, 65% Magomedov in the field, and the three sharp panels split between the two men.
FLAG — the host gave this method split without stating its total, so the usual reconciliation check could not run; 45 is the sum of the counts he read out.
The best method panel is split four ways, one vote to each of KO and decision for Delano and KO and submission for Magomedov.
Women's flyweight. Not one channel picked a KO, and the best method predictors go the other way from the field — 2 of 3 have Fernandes by decision.
Heavyweight; Lorenco's UFC debut. The field is 56% the debutant while every sharp panel is on Petersen — the host puts that down to Petersen alternating wins and losses.
Featherweight prelim headliner; Nakamura won the Road to UFC tournament this year.
The best method predictors were unanimous on a Nakamura KO, but the host never gave the panel's size for this fight, so no method-panel count is recorded.
Flyweight; opens the main card and Degli's UFC debut. The best method predictors are on a submission that only 19% of the field picked, and that the oddsmakers rate behind a decision.
Women's bantamweight. 91% of the method votes have Milosevic finishing it.
The host said the best method predictors were split between her KO and her submission but gave no panel size, so no method-panel count is recorded.
Light heavyweight. The host's second best bet: the best predictors and best favorite-pickers are 100% on Fernando, though the method panel splits evenly between his KO (+155) and his decision (+200).
Bantamweight, and a 16-year age gap: Grant is 40, Smith 24.
The host names the lone dissenter across all three sharp panels as Axel MMA, on Grant.
Also one of his best bets, on Smith's moneyline — but note 2 of the 3 best method predictors have the +255 underdog winning.
Women's strawweight co-main, No. 2 against No. 3. Not one channel picked a KO.
The field is 82% Suarez but the best predictors are only 4 of 7 — the widest field-versus-sharps gap on the card.
The best method predictors were unanimous on Suarez by decision, but the host gave no panel size, so no method-panel count is recorded.
Heavyweight main event, moved up after Sean Brady withdrew.
94% of the method votes have this ending by KO either way, and the best method panel agrees unanimously on that — only on who. Cortes-Acosta by KO pays -114 against his -225 moneyline.
The field is 76% Cortes-Acosta but the best predictors are 4 of 7 and the best favorite-pickers are dead even.
